html:
The Pechenegs were a semi-nomadic Turkic people from Central Asia who controlled the steppes north of the Black Sea in the 900s and 1000s. On the map for 900 they are in what is now eastern Ukraine.

Pushed west by other nomads, they reached the Dnieper and Don in the late 800s. Around 895, in league with the Bulgarians, they attacked the Magyars and drove them west, which led to the Magyar settlement of Hungary.

They lived by herding and raiding, and sold their help to the highest bidder. Emperor Constantine VII advised his son to keep them as friends, because they could block Rus traders at the Dnieper rapids. There in 972 they killed Prince Sviatoslav of Kievan Rus', and their khan made a drinking cup of his skull. For their later history see Pechenegs around 1000.
sum: The Pechenegs were a semi-nomadic Turkic people from Central Asia who controlled the steppes north of the Black Sea in the 900s and 1000s. On the map for 900 they are in what is now eastern Ukraine.
